symptoms: Dark brown concentric rings (target-like spots) on older leaves, yellow halo around lesions, stem cankers, lower leaf drop.
cause: Fungal pathogen thriving in warm temperatures (24-29°C) and heavy dew or rain.
organicRemedy: Spray Neem oil (5ml/L) or copper oxychloride 50 WP (2.5g/L). Apply Trichoderma viride (10g/L) to soil and foliage. Remove affected lower leaves.
chemicalTreatment: Mancozeb 75 WP (2g/L) or Chlorothalonil 75 WP (2g/L) or Azoxystrobin 23 SC (1ml/L). Repeat at 10-14 day intervals.
preventiveMeasures: Practice 3-year crop rotation, stake tomato plants to improve air circulation, avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation, use disease-free certified seeds.

symptoms: Water-soaked dark lesions on leaf tips, white fungal growth on underside in humid mornings, rapid browning and collapse of foliage, brown blotches on fruit.
cause: Oomycete pathogen favored by cool, foggy/wet weather (15-22°C with >90% humidity).
organicRemedy: Bordeaux mixture (1%), copper hydroxide spray. Immediate destruction of severely infected plants. Compost tea foliar spray.
chemicalTreatment: Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP (2.5g/L) or Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP (3g/L) or Dimethomorph (1g/L).
preventiveMeasures: Monitor local weather forecasts for blight warnings, plant resistant hybrids (e.g. Arka Rakshak), ensure rapid field drainage.

symptoms: Upward curling, puckering, thickening of leaves, stunting of plants, yellowing between veins, drastically reduced fruit set.
cause: Geminivirus transmitted primarily by Whitefly (Bemisia tabaci).
organicRemedy: Install yellow sticky traps (15-20 per acre) to trap whiteflies. Spray Neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%) or Verticillium lecanii (5g/L).
chemicalTreatment: Control vector with Imidacloprid 17.8 SL (0.5ml/L) or Diafenthiuron 50 WP (1g/L) or Spiromesifen 22.9 SC (1ml/L).
preventiveMeasures: Grow barrier crops like maize/sorghum on border, use 40-mesh insect netting in nursery, remove weed hosts around field.

symptoms: Yellowish-orange pustules arranged in parallel linear stripes on leaf blades, powdery yellow spores rub off on fingers.
cause: Fungal spore dispersal during cool humid winters (10-15°C with heavy dew).
organicRemedy: Early morning spray of bio-fungicide Bacillus subtilis or sour buttermilk spray (50ml/L).
chemicalTreatment: Propiconazole 25 EC (1ml/L) or Tebuconazole 25.9 EC (1ml/L) spray as soon as first stripe appears. Spray 200L solution/acre.
preventiveMeasures: Sow rust-resistant varieties like DBW-187, DBW-303, HD-3226; avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization; timely sowing before Nov 20.

symptoms: Water-soaked stripes along leaf margins turning yellow-white with wavy margins, milky bacterial ooze beads on young lesions in morning.
cause: Bacterium entering through hydathodes/wounds, aggravated by heavy rain, high winds, and excess urea application.
organicRemedy: Spray fresh cow dung filtrate (20%) or Pseudomonas fluorescens (5g/L) twice at 15-day interval.
chemicalTreatment: Copper oxychloride (2.5g/L) mixed with Streptocycline (0.1g/L) or Plantomycin (1g/L).
preventiveMeasures: Drain standing water temporarily, balance nitrogen with higher potassium (MOP), avoid clipping seedling tips during transplanting.

symptoms: Spindle-shaped elliptical lesions with gray/white center and brown/reddish borders on leaf blades, neck rot causing white empty panicles.
cause: Favored by night temperatures around 20°C, high humidity (>90%), and prolonged leaf wetness.
organicRemedy: Foliar spray of Trichoderma harzianum or Panchagavya (30ml/L).
chemicalTreatment: Tricyclazole 75 WP (0.6g/L) or Isoprothiolane 40 EC (1.5ml/L) or Kasugamycin 3% SL (2ml/L).
preventiveMeasures: Treat seeds with Carbendazim (2g/kg), split nitrogen fertilizer into 3-4 doses, maintain proper plant spacing.

symptoms: Rosetted flowers, double seeds, internal feeding in developing bolls, stained lint, premature boll opening.
cause: Nocturnal moth larvae boring into floral buds and developing bolls.
organicRemedy: Install pheromone traps (5-8 traps/acre) for monitoring, release Trichogramma egg parasitoids (60,000/acre), neem oil spray.
chemicalTreatment: Profenofos 50 EC (2ml/L) or Emamectin Benzoate 5 SG (0.5g/L) or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC (0.3ml/L).
preventiveMeasures: Synchronized planting, terminate crop by January, avoid ratoon cotton, deep summer ploughing to expose pupae.

symptoms: Hard, black irregular sclerotia adhering tightly to tuber skin (dirt that won't wash off), stem cankers, aerial tubers.
cause: Soil-borne and seed-borne fungus favored by cool, wet soils at planting.
organicRemedy: Seed tuber dip in Trichoderma viride (10g/L water) for 30 minutes before sowing. Apply neem cake (100kg/acre) in soil.
chemicalTreatment: Tuber treatment with Moncut / Flutolanil (2ml/kg) or Pencycuron (2.5ml/kg) or Azoxystrobin (2.5ml/kg) prior to cold storage or planting.
preventiveMeasures: Plant certified seed tubers, practice green manuring with dhaincha, allow tubers to mature and skin to harden before harvest.

symptoms: Circular sunken spots on ripe fruits with concentric rings of black acervuli, straw-colored shriveled dried fruits, dieback of twigs.
cause: Fungal infection during humid rainy weather and high temperatures (28-30°C).
organicRemedy: Spray cow urine (10%) fermented with neem leaves or Pseudomonas fluorescens (10g/L).
chemicalTreatment: Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC (1ml/L) or Captan 50 WP (2.5g/L) or Tebuconazole 25.9 EC (1ml/L).
preventiveMeasures: Seed treatment with Thiram (3g/kg), collect and burn diseased fruits, avoid excessive shade in nursery.

symptoms: Window-pane leaf skeletonization, pinholes in young whorls, heavy sawdust-like frass inside whorls, ragged leaf edges.
cause: Invasive pest larvae feeding aggressively in the central funnel of the plant.
organicRemedy: Application of sand + wood ash (9:1) into whorls, Metarhizium rileyi or Beauveria bassiana (5g/L) spray, pheromone traps.
chemicalTreatment: Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC (0.4ml/L) or Spinetoram 11.7 SC (0.5ml/L) directed straight into whorls using knapsack sprayer.
preventiveMeasures: Deep summer tillage, intercropping with pulses (cowpea/pigeon pea), push-pull technology with Napier grass.

symptoms: Vibrant green uniform pigmentation, clean leaf margins, robust turgor pressure, active vegetative growth, no signs of pathogen damage.
cause: Optimal soil moisture, balanced nutrition, and active photosynthesis.
organicRemedy: Maintain preventative health with Seaweed extract (2ml/L) or Jeevamrutha foliar spray every 15 days.
chemicalTreatment: No chemical application required. Continue regular scouting and balanced micronutrient spray.
preventiveMeasures: Follow integrated pest and disease management (IPM), maintain balanced drip fertigation schedule.
